name: Manhattan
description: Rye or bourbon stirred with sweet vermouth and bitters—silky, aromatic, and unmistakably classic.
history: A late-19th-century New York classic that helped define the stirred whiskey cocktail. The best versions stay dry enough that vermouth supports the whiskey rather than smothering it.
whyItWorks: Vermouth’s herbal sweetness rounds whiskey while Angostura ties spice and oak together. Stirring keeps the texture polished.
steps: Add rye, sweet vermouth, and bitters to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until well chilled, about 25–30 seconds.
Garnish with a cocktail cherry, or a lemon peel if you prefer brightness.
techniqueNotes: A 2:1 whiskey-to-vermouth ratio keeps the drink whiskey-forward.
Bourbon yields a rounder Manhattan; rye stays spicier and drier.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Bright spice and structure—the classic Manhattan backbone.
Slightly richer rye character with oak depth.
If using bourbon, Russell’s Reserve keeps the drink balanced and composed.

substitutions.notes: Bourbon Manhattan is softer and sweeter.
